title: A teleost-specific oxygen-immunity axis where FIH activates NF-kappaB via competitive IkappaBalpha binding.
authors: Zhan, Zhipeng; Liang, Mincong; Yu, Yang; Cui, Yangchi; Li, Zhimin; Pan, Weiqiang; Zhou, Ziyi; Jiang, Lai; Hou, Yafeng; He, Jian; Wu, Kun; Weng, Shaoping; He, Jianguo; Guo, Changjun
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文研究鱼类FIH通过竞争性结合IkappaBalpha激活NF-kappaB的氧-免疫轴，涉及蛋白-DNA互作（NF-kappaB-DNA）与AlphaFold3结构建模，但核心是蛋白-蛋白竞争结合而非TF-DNA特异性识别，方法上仅用结构预测无AI/物理模拟深度建模，故为中档匹配。
abstract: Global warming-induced aquatic deoxygenation poses a severe physiological challenge to teleosts, often influencing their immune defense mechanisms. While aquatic organisms are under evolutionary pressure to balance metabolic adaptation with pathogen resistance, the molecular strategies they employ to overcome high pathogen loads under hypoxic stress remain poorly understood. Here, an oxygen-immunity regulatory axis was identified in teleosts, in which the oxygen sensor FIH (factor inhibiting HIF) activated the NF-kappaB pathway by competitively displacing p65 from IkappaBalpha. Experiments with FIH mutants showed that NF-kappaB activation did not require FIH hydroxylase activity. In vitro, FIH bound IkappaBalpha, promoted p65 nuclear translocation, and increased inflammatory gene expression. FIH knockdown blunted these responses. In vivo, CRISPR/Cas9-generated drfih(-/-) zebrafish showed reduced NF-kappaB-driven inflammation, altered responses to LPS challenge, and a dose-dependent trade-off in Vibrio anguillarum infection, with reduced resistance at a low dose but mitigated immunopathology at a high dose. AlphaFold3 modeling and mutational analyses pinpointed a competitive interface. In human cells, FIH-IkappaBalpha binding occurred without NF-kappaB activation. Notably, replacing a C-terminal segment of human IkappaBalpha with the teleost counterpart restored FIH-dependent competition and NF-kappaB activation, indicating lineage-specific structural divergence. Extensive cross-species predictions revealed that several aquatic vertebrates, an amphibian, and a shrimp species possessed a competitive interface, whereas the terrestrial species examined did not. These findings revealed a hydroxylase-independent mechanism, likely associated with aquatic lineages, that linked oxygen sensing to innate immunity and had implications for vertebrate evolution, climate-driven hypoxia, and aquaculture health.
abstract_zh: 全球变暖引起的水体脱氧对硬骨鱼类构成严峻的生理挑战，常影响其免疫防御机制。尽管水生生物在进化压力下需平衡代谢适应与病原体抵抗，但它们在低氧胁迫下应对高病原体负荷所采用的分子策略仍知之甚少。本研究在硬骨鱼类中鉴定出一条氧-免疫调控轴，其中氧传感器FIH（因子抑制HIF）通过竞争性取代p65与IkappaBalpha的结合来激活NF-kappaB通路。FIH突变体实验表明，NF-kappaB激活不依赖FIH羟化酶活性。体外实验中，FIH结合IkappaBalpha，促进p65核转位，并增加炎症基因表达；FIH敲低则削弱这些反应。体内实验中，CRISPR/Cas9生成的drfih(-/-)斑马鱼表现出NF-kappaB驱动的炎症减少、对LPS刺激的反应改变，以及在鳗弧菌感染中的剂量依赖性权衡，即低剂量时抵抗力降低，但高剂量时免疫病理损伤减轻。AlphaFold3建模和突变分析定位了一个竞争性界面。在人类细胞中，FIH-IkappaBalpha结合发生但不激活NF-kappaB。值得注意的是，将人类IkappaBalpha的C端片段替换为硬骨鱼对应片段，恢复了FIH依赖性竞争和NF-kappaB激活，表明存在谱系特异性结构分化。广泛的跨物种预测显示，多种水生脊椎动物、一种两栖动物和一种虾类具有竞争性界面，而所检视的陆生物种则不具备。这些发现揭示了一种不依赖羟化酶的机制，可能与水生物种谱系相关，将氧感知与先天免疫联系起来，并对脊椎动物进化、气候驱动的低氧及水产养殖健康具有启示意义。
